source: Measured through `ale validate` (pinned engine bfb7505), run validate-3f6c0b60 of 2026-11-25 on the tree of 4f91966: the oracle episode ran the reference controller (solution/reference: privileged tips in place of perception, rate commands through the public wire) on the fixed hidden set (tests/hidden/procedures.json: 12 procedures x 800 steps, generator endosim-procedure/0.2) in the engine's separate verifier sandbox, Isaac Sim 6.2.0.0 rendering on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (not a cloud-listed GPU model), driver 535.183.01 (below Omniverse RTX's R550 floor; the renderer's driver check is off, the canary found 10 of 10 markers within 1.10 px), rootless Docker 29.10.1 with the CPUs limited by affinity instead of a quota (tests/README.md section 7). Its verification.json: useful_view_fraction 0.9030208 (8669 of 9600 steps; per procedure 0.939 0.866 0.953 0.925 0.878 0.913 0.836 0.934 0.873 0.928 0.926 0.868), probe pairs 179 of 555 differing (the lock's fraction is 0.1), no aborted procedure, no lens contact, ratio 1.00002, reward 1.0. The same mean as the native run of the same task files on an RTX 6000 Ada, driver 570.195.03 (763919b: 0.9030208, 163 of 589 pairs). The reference reads the simulator's state and never the picture, so the value does not depend on the renderer, but it depends a little on which steps are probed (the memory it keeps after a repeated step is the copy's about one time in ten): over ten draws of the probes the render-free loop (tests/review/fast_eval.py's sessions) gave 0.9029 to 0.9037. full_at 0.98: the spread over probe draws is below 0.1 %; the margin also covers a threshold flipped by rounding on another CPU (the numerics are not pinned).
